transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I’ve been tapped for something huge at work and in town, like I’m the only one who really understands what’s going on and everyone else just needs to catch up to me. It's like I've been chosen for a critical role to protect things, and I'm just waiting for everyone else to operate on my level.
How has your sleep been lately? Have you felt like you need much less sleep than usual but still have plenty of energy?

Yes, there are weeks where I'll only sleep two or three hours a night, but I don't feel tired at all. Instead, I feel completely supercharged, like sleep is just a waste of time and my body doesn't even need it. I'll spend those late-night hours tinkering with network configs, reading security blogs, or sketching out flowcharts on the kitchen counter.
Have you ever had periods in the past where you felt the exact opposite—feeling very down, exhausted, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yes, I do have those down times, and it feels like the color has been completely turned off in my life, leaving me with this heavy, gray hopelessness. I lose all interest in things I used to love, like hiking, tinkering with my home servers, or leading worship at church. These low stretches have been coming and going for about the last seven months.
When you experience these periods of high energy, sleeping very little, and feeling chosen for this special role, how long do they typically last at a time?
Those high-energy phases usually last for weeks at a time when they hit. They've been cycling back and forth like that for well over a year and a half now.
Do you ever have these thoughts about being chosen or having a special role during times when your mood feels completely normal, and you are neither in a high nor a low phase?

Yes, definitely. Even during times when my mood is flat and I'm just going through the motions, I still hold onto those beliefs about my role and being monitored. It doesn't seem to go away just because my energy levels are back to normal.
When your mood is flat or normal, how long do these thoughts about your special role or being monitored usually last? Have they ever lasted for two weeks or more continuously during these times?

Yes, they definitely last for weeks at a time. Even when my mood is completely flat and I'm just going through the motions, I will still hear that metallic voice at night and firmly believe certain executives are monitoring me for two or more weeks straight.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ['F25', 'F31']. The patient has now confirmed that psychotic symptoms, specifically auditory hallucinations (a metallic voice) and persecutory/grandiose delusions (being monitored by executives, having a special role), persist for two weeks or more during periods of normal or flat mood (euthymia). This meets the key criterion for Schizoaffective disorder (F25) and rules out Bipolar affective disorder with psychotic features (F31), where psychotic symptoms would only occur during active mood episodes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with concurrent symptoms of both mood episodes (manic episodes characterized by decreased need for sleep and high energy, and major depressive episodes characterized by hopelessness and anhedonia) and active-phase symptoms of schizophrenia (auditory hallucinations of a metallic voice, and delusions of grandeur and persecution). Crucially, the patient confirms that the psychotic symptoms (hearing the voice and believing they are being monitored) persist for at least two weeks in the absence of any prominent mood symptoms, which fulfills the diagnostic criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder (ICD-10: F25).
